steps.title: Access Developer Settings
steps.action: Click profile picture > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App.
steps.actorReason: Requires logged-in user with appropriate permissions.
steps.text: Navigate to the developer settings in the GitHub console to register a new application.

steps.title: Configure App Details
steps.action: Enter the Application name, Homepage URL, and Authorization callback URL.
steps.actorReason: Developer must provide their own project-specific URLs.
steps.text: Fill in the required fields for the application, including the redirect URI provided by the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Register Application
steps.actorReason: Form submission is required by the user.
steps.text: Complete the creation process to receive your Client ID.

steps.title: Generate Client Secret
steps.action: Click Generate a new client secret.
steps.actorReason: Secrets must be generated and managed by the user.
steps.text: Create a client secret after registration to allow authentication.

steps.title: Connect to Composio
steps.action: Paste Client ID and Client Secret into the auth config.

steps.text: Navigate to the Composio dashboard to create an auth config using your newly created GitHub credentials.
steps.quote: Register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.

faq.question: Does Composio support GitHub Apps?
faq.answer:
Yes. You can bring your own GitHub App by configuring its client ID and client secret in the GitHub auth config.

The GitHub App installation step is separate from the OAuth credential setup. The user still needs to install the GitHub App on the relevant account or organization and grant repository access before GitHub App based tool calls can work. GitHub App permissions come from the app's GitHub settings and installation grant, not from auth config scopes.
